report:
Fresh source review of the complete claim and all current associations. The four obligations are visibility of unknown work, stable Sage/metadata operation families, raw diagnostic ingredients retained in unmapped query keys when semantic projection is unavailable, and rejection of unexpected fallback by checked closed dependency claims.

The ordinary src/inspector.rs association identifies the adapter importing build_dynamic_trace. LiveInspectionProvider::record takes the inspection log, projects every supplied event, stores the returned children in RunObservation, and run returns that stored observation without removing unmapped nodes. The ordinary crates/sage-host/src/trace.rs association supplies the actual projection: QueryEnter and QueryLeaf move the original key into TraceKey::Unmapped; QueryExit attaches the completed node and does not strip its key. query_operation strips parenthesized arguments and surrounding whitespace from the family only. A key without parentheses still becomes an unmapped node with its original ingredient. ExternalMetadata keeps the complete operation string as ingredient while using the prefix as its family. Semantic phase/span events keep their producer-authored operation names. attach_trace_node retains nested as well as root work; unordered normalization only sorts. Outstanding stack nodes are drained, and malformed exits add visible unmapped recorder-error diagnostics. Executed, validated, reused and cancelled dispositions remain represented. The protocol's tagged TraceKey representation explicitly serializes Unmapped and its ingredient. snapshot_trace normalizes the ingredient to its operation for deterministic test snapshots; live Inspector record uses build_dynamic_trace directly, so that separate normalization does not erase its raw diagnostics.

The third implementation entry is explicitly TODO in sage_meta::todo, service_spec.rs. It accurately states that closed dependency claim checking is absent, and requires an API accepting the complete projected trace and allowed operations, recursively rejecting unexpected unmapped query/metadata nodes without filtering. This narrow implementation deferral is justified and remains visibly deferred: the ordinary projection entries establish retention, not closed-check enforcement. No claim of full implementation is made.

The complete associated test set contains only sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_unknown_work. The entire body consists of TODO comments and supplies no executable assertions. It explicitly defers real-trace evidence for all balanced Salsa requests and metadata calls, plus tests preventing forbidden-demand checks from filtering unknown nodes. It names the missing complete-trace checking API as prerequisite and requires nested unexpected queries and metadata scenarios. Accepting this TODO does not claim any test coverage or successful enforcement. To close it, associated source-driven trace tests must assert retained raw ingredients and stable operation families, and checker tests must demonstrate rejection of unexpected nested fallback. No N/A entries exist.

All requirements are accounted for by current ordinary projection evidence or the explicit implementation/test deferrals. No additional edits are requested for this review refresh. Ran cargo meta review start/read and inspected the current captured implementation, complete test body, association metadata, and protocol dependency; behavior suites are centrally owned by root and were not run by this reviewer. No Rust source was changed and no reproduced behavioral failure is claimed.
